[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Engage in physical exercise: Helps release endorphins, reduces stress and anxiety, improves physical health, boosts self-esteem and confidence, and fosters mental clarity and emotional resilience.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Practicing gratitude: Reminding oneself of things to be grateful for increases positive emotions and promotes resilience in tough times.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Engage in hobbies and passions: Helps reduce stress, improve mood, boost self-esteem, and provide a sense of accomplishment and confidence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Seek support: Seeking support from trusted loved ones or a therapist provides a non-judgmental space to talk about difficulties and develop new skills for increasing resilience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tips for staying motivated in the face of difficulties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Focus on your goals: Keep goals in mind, remind yourself why you started, and set smaller, achievable goals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Take breaks: Permission to take breaks when tired or overwhelmed; suggested activities include walking, stretching, or listening to music.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Visualize success: Visualizing oneself succeeding and overcoming obstacles can help motivate towards desired outcomes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Keep a positive attitude: Monitor self-talk, replace negative self-talk with positive affirmations, and celebrate progress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Seek support: Connect with people who can provide encouragement, share goals with friends, family, or a mentor, and consider joining a support group or online community.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Stay accountable: Set up a system of accountability to keep motivated, such as sharing goals and progress with a coach or friend.
